claude_proposed_widenings.name: passive_trigger (class feature family)
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Relentless Rage fires automatically when a specific game-state condition is met (drop to 0 HP while Rage is active). This is not a player-initiated activation — there is no activationCost of free or bonus_action. The existing 'activation' family models deliberate player-turn choices; a new family is needed for features that fire in response to external state events.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: If you drop to 0 Hit Points while your Rage is active and don't die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: escalating_save_dc (resource type)
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The DC starts at 10 and increases by 5 per use within a rest period, then resets on Short or Long Rest. This is not a use-count cap — it is a mutable save DC tracked per rest. UseCountResource and UseCountCap have no representation for this pattern.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: Each time you use this feature after the first, the DC increases by 5. When you finish a Short or Long Rest, the DC resets to 10.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: set_hp (effect atom)
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The on-success outcome sets HP to a specific derived value (2 × Barbarian level). This is distinct from heal_hp which adds HP to the current total. A set_hp effect atom is needed to model HP-floor or HP-set operations.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: your Hit Points instead change to a number equal to twice your Barbarian level

claude_proposed_widenings.name: trigger_condition (class-feature trigger shape)
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The trigger is conditioned on two simultaneous facts: HP dropped to 0, AND Rage is active. The surface has no type for compound state-condition triggers on class features.
